question: Do trained LightGBM and quantile-TCN models improve daily unit-sales forecasts over seasonal naive for UCI Online Retail II products?
target: daily fulfilled positive units per StockCode (unit-sales, not unconstrained demand)

data.note: 2011-12-09 is a partial trading day and is excluded

cohort.rule: uses only sales on or before selection_end; requires 56 days of history

refit_policy: each origin refits on labels available on or before that origin (operational walk-forward)
selection_rule: lowest mean validation pinball (average of q10/q50/q90) across validation origins; TCN averaged over seeds; validation origins precede every test origin
postprocessing: negative values clipped to 0 and quantiles sorted, applied identically to all models after measuring raw crossing
metrics: MASE (seasonal-7 scale from history up to origin; undefined reported)
paired per-series bootstrap of MAE differences
supersedes: 1.0.0 (its seasonal-naive baseline repeated older weeks beyond horizon 7: audit F01)
honesty_note: Not an untouched holdout: protocol 1.0.0 already looked at both windows (2011-10-13 as a validation origin, 2011-11-10 as the test origin). 2.0.0 keeps the same search grid and selection rule and makes no new tuning choice after seeing results; it is a corrected re-run with rolling origins, reported as such, not as a new confirmatory test. Differences whose 95% interval includes zero are reported as 'no clear difference detected' (no equivalence test was run).
